subject: Archaeology
title: Schliemann Finds Troy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Schliemann Finds Troy usable.

hook.text: Everyone said Troy was a myth. Heinrich Schliemann bet his fortune it was real — and started digging.

buildup.text: Using Homer's Iliad as a guide, Schliemann identified a hill in Turkey called Hisarlik in 1868.

discovery.text: He found not one city but nine, layered on top of each other across thousands of years.

twist.text: Schliemann blasted through layers with dynamite, destroying priceless evidence in his rush for gold.

climax.text: He claimed to find Priam's treasure, but it came from a city 1,000 years older than Homer's Troy.

punchline.text: He found Troy but destroyed much of it in the process.

quiz.question: What major mistake did Schliemann make while excavating Troy?
options: He dug at the wrong site entirely
He destroyed layers with dynamite, losing priceless evidence
He refused to share his findings with other scholars
